forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Dartford: Orchard Theatre forecasts overspend, with extra funding request due at November Cabinet
news_drafts.lead:
Dartford Council's Cabinet papers for 29 October show the Orchard Theatre project is forecasting an overspend against its approved budget. A request for additional funding will go to Cabinet in November. The paper gives no figure. It says the theatre remains on track to reopen as scheduled, with partial practical completion on 6 December and some elements still to finish.

The temporary Orchard West theatre is forecast to overspend its £360,000 budget, which is paid for from money set aside (reserves), by £95,000. Projected spend is £455,000, and £453,730 had been incurred by the end of September. Air conditioning costs of £100,000 are excluded from the estimate. The paper says the overspend will be considered at the full projection exercise, with a view to offsetting it against underspends elsewhere this year.

In council housing, the housing revenue account (the separate, ring-fenced account for the council's own homes, paid for by rents) has a projected deficit of £497,610 for 2026/27 in the mid-year projection, against £659,090 in the current budget. Repairs and maintenance is projected to be overspent by £500,000, including extra delivery costs for the outgoing contractor, TSG Building Services PLC. The paper says the overspend has no significant impact on the account's ongoing viability. Roof renewals are forecast to overspend by about £0.300m, which the council says is needed to keep its housing stock compliant. An anticipated underspend on window replacement is expected to offset it.

findings.paper_title: Procurement Update (Waivers Procurement Strategy and Social Value) Covering Report Nov26
findings.headline: The social value central log lists 18 projects, and 6 of the 27 projects run by the Procurement Team from April to September 2026 have social value built into their specifications, assessment or contract conditions.
findings.detail: The log was created in July 2025 and records the quality questions asked in tenders, contractor responses, obligations and targets, review dates and achievements. The social value obligations in the 6 projects fall into five groups, with working with local schools and colleges the most common (6 projects).
findings.matters: A council that records the social value it has contracted for, and reports on it annually, is showing how it tracks non-price benefits in its contract spend, which other councils comparing procurement practice can measure against.

findings.headline: Two of four social value action points are late, with target dates of October 2025 and March 2026 now slipping.
findings.detail: Action 3.1, stakeholder engagement, slipped from its October 2025 target because of its complexity and the number of departments involved. A consultation approved by Cabinet on 29 October 2026 is expected to conclude before the end of December 2026. Action 3.2, the Social Value Policy, had a March 2026 target and a draft has been prepared, with the final version awaiting the consultation results.
findings.matters: Social value commitments written into contracts are a tool for value for money, and a late policy shows how far the council's framework for setting and tracking those commitments has yet to be finished.

findings.paper_title: Procurement Update (Waivers Procurement Strategy and Social Value) Covering Report Nov26
findings.headline: Procurement waivers approved in April to September 2026 numbered 13, against 27 in April to September 2025 and 15 in October 2025 to March 2026.
findings.detail: The paper reports 12 below-threshold Director Discretion waivers and 1 Urgency and Emergency waiver in the latest period. The April to September 2025 period included 3 above-threshold Direct Award waivers, and the two later periods list none. The paper gives the reasons as Specialist Requirement (7), Incumbent Contractor (4), Lack of Competition (1) and Urgency/Emergency (1).
findings.matters: Waivers are the exception route around competitive tendering, so a falling count, and no above-threshold direct awards in the later periods, bears directly on the control environment that auditors and lenders look at.
findings.figures: 27 waivers (April 2025 to September 2025); 15 waivers (October 2025 to March 2026); 13 waivers (April 2026 to September 2026); 3 above-threshold Direct Award waivers (April 2025 to September 2025); 12 below-threshold Director Discretion waivers and 1 Urgency and Emergency waiver (April 2026 to September 2026)

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Dartford Sevenoaks EQA Final report 060826
findings.headline: A stakeholder reports that staffing difficulties meant internal audit 'focus[ed] more on delivering the basics', with less work on LGR and assets transfer.
findings.detail: The stakeholder says they would have valued more internal audit work on local government reorganisation, asset transfer and related activity. The assessor reports this as one stakeholder's view.
findings.matters: A finance director at a council going through reorganisation will want to know whether internal audit capacity is going to the transition work.
findings.quote: Because of staffing difficulties, internal audit has had to focus more on delivering the basics. We would have valued more work on LGR, assets transfer and other related activity.
